column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3f, the oldest source for belief, test and after; its step (v), verification, is why each moment ends on a dated test (K curve, T 27 and 29 Sep runs, C the 30 Sep bar), all facts as in RANKING_5 and BLIND_POOL_3.
Mon 16 Nov: same Dewey chapter as row 1; the felt-difficulty trigger and step (v) verification are already inside row 1's five steps, so one Dewey row in the store.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing paragraph, the moments reach different depths (K process, T and C premise); adds Mezirow's content-process-premise split, which Q27's levels lack; year of the chapter still to be found before any citation.

Mon 16 Nov: same Mezirow chapter; the trigger-event idea adds little beyond Dewey's felt difficulty (row 1), and exactly overclaims for T, where the team priced the critics' view and kept its frame rather than redefining the problem.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f copout, REFLECT credits the objection put as an alternative explanation and the team's own default examined, which matches BLIND_POOL_3 E1's before and after (VT a sensible default, then why it suits Laura); one scored example, not the rubric table.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing paragraph, the credit goes to what the lesson commits the writer to, so each moment ends on the part of the plan it still governs (RANKING_5's own rule); one scored SDC example, so cite as an example, near Q27-006 (DEAL's last step).

Mon 16 Nov: 3f every moment; re-read at source today (assessors see only interpretative descriptions, a serious threat to validity; their guideline: objective information about the triggering situation to verify); Caplet's dated register figures answer the marker's main doubt.
Mon 16 Nov: Koole's remedy (process skills, objective information about the triggering situation) is the basis of row 7's use; quote re-read at source today; one Koole row.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f, research basis for standing order 21's rule that a reason found later is told as what the team understands now (Koole: hindsight and introspection bias go undetected; re-read at source today); evidence for an existing rule, not a new one.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f set, evidence for three moments and for moving buying it to 2.5 (17.7 against 20.7-21.7, RANKING_5); abstract re-read today (weighted averaging, presenters do not anticipate, seven studies), full paper unread so S 3; holds for items judged together as one set.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard only, never defend three moments with a rule of three; Nordmo and Selart re-read today (198 students; four claims liked more than two; claim count did not move scepticism) but Shu and Carlson second-hand, so S 3.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f, the practical case for depth over breadth; the six words match WHARTON_NORTH_STAR l.145-146 exactly, but the use column then says five words: say six (the Team Reflection paragraph's own list, l.129-130, has five, without uncertainty); Keel inference, so S 3.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f placement, an admission helps only after competence is shown, so 3f last; re-read at source today (48 male sophomores, 30.2 and -2.5, F=10.33 df 1/40, the pratfall alone insignificant); replaces H5-015's second-hand version; liking, not credibility.

Mon 16 Nov: the authors' untested explanation of row 13 (quotes re-read today); its 2.5 use is weak, since the mis-click is told without attribution (Book 18), so it is not a competent person's blunder; harmless is not in the record (the order was cancelled, then re-placed at 15:22).

Mon 16 Nov: 3f T, which kind of mistake, not whether; checked at source today, Table 3 Study 1 (N=200, 7-point scale): perceived integrity 5.32 apology against 4.27 denial after a competence lapse, 2.73 against 4.39 after an integrity lapse; say rated integrity, since rated competence barely moved (4.56 against 4.46).
Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard, why one owned slip does not sink a report that shows skill elsewhere and why nothing may look like hiding; the reason for row 15, kept as a separate guard.
Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard, every admission must match the dated record a judge can check (the copout a decision kept, the fills told as timing, as E1 and E3 say); Study 2 N=444 confirmed at source today.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f T, owning the first plan's drop as the team's own decision reads as control; release re-read today (14 firms, three industries, 21 years, 14 to 19 percent), paper unread, correlation only, so S 3.
Mon 16 Nov: the release's mechanism quote (more in control; outside attributions did not predict outcomes), re-read today; same source and use as row 18, so one row carries both.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f T; abstract only (re-read today), so S 3; stealing thunder needs a risk the evaluator learns it elsewhere, and the 27 Sep failure appears nowhere a judge could find it while IPS l.9 already tells the switch, so use only the second finding: accepting responsibility beat blaming others.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard, each admission's figure must be exact and register-sourced; re-read today (F=26.31 is negative against positive persuasion on scepticism), but the paper's degrees of freedom do not fit N=198 and its negatives were claims against a company, not self-admissions.
Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard, a token flaw earns nothing from an effortful reader such as a judge; abstract only, consumer products, so S 3.
Mon 16 Nov: 3f guard, an admission chosen to look humble reads as performance, so each must be the cause of a rule still in the plan; abstract only, an essay with no readers tested, so S 3.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f and 2.5, most institutional investors judge by results, the setting for row 31's contrast; abstract only, so S 3; near Q13-006 (outcome bias in the lab) and H9-175, but the first investor record in the store.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f C context; re-read at source today (non-performance attributes drive recommendations; slightly under six extra recommendations against half of one; 91% of the US consulting market, about $3 trillion); the paper itself says its soft investment factors relate to the investment process.

Mon 16 Nov: checked at source today: 6.31% against 7.43% (-1.12%) is equal-weighted only and, in the authors' words, fund scale seems fully to explain it (it disappears with size controls); value-weighted, no significant gap; the paper finds recommendations in general add no value and never tests process-based picks against performance-based ones; never say judging by process cost 1.12% a year.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f C, at most one sentence on what switching on returns costs investors, told as what the team understands now (RANKING_5); abstract only, and it shows new money went to later losers, not that sponsors chased returns, so S 3.
Mon 16 Nov: 3f, claim 4 changed to a hybrid of a dated process and an honest result; quotes re-read at source today (ossify into bureaucratic rituals; process-outcome hybrids; rigor and accuracy).

Mon 16 Nov: quotes re-read today, but the source says outcome accountability protects dissenters by judging accuracy, while C was settled by a process bar set before the objection; keep the moment's guard (the teammate never the fool, bar of 30 Sep before the 5 Oct objection, both E1) and drop the claim that this finding supports it.

Mon 16 Nov: guard on how claim 4 is argued, never rest it on escalation experiments; atlas re-read today (outcome recorded failed; no effects of accountability; a stronger manipulation and larger sample), replication itself unopened, so S 3.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f K and 2.5 aha beside row 24; both quotes match WHARTON_NORTH_STAR (l.143-144 criterion; l.197-198 Guide p.5), but only the first is addressed to evaluators, the Guide line tells teams not to rewrite, so drop twice and tells its evaluators for the pair; near H9-175 (Guide p.3), this row is the stronger current wording.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing paragraph, learning not results, all three moments dated before any order (E1, E3, E4, E6); fix the page: may evolve as you learn more is Guide p.1, not p.2 (filed Guide text), and it is not in WHARTON_NORTH_STAR; p.5's half is Q27-004 and quoted accurately.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f, reflection on action, so reasons found later are labelled as now (already row 9 and standing order 21); drop the feelings the use column gives the team (an unpleasant surprise, a pleasant surprise with a sting), which the record does not show, and the claim that T reframed ends (the floor stayed).
